adopted..claude/skills/update-muthur/: this skill. The source has renamed it three times (sync-upstream, sync-agent-infra, sync-muthur, update-muthur) and ships it as an unhydrated stub; the local copy carries the same name and watermark filename it has there, and a hydrated procedure. So what lands from a commit touching this path is the procedure's own changes, never the stub framing. The name travels because the verb is `npm update`'s — what gets updated is the vendored copy in whatever tree the command runs in — which reads the same at every link in the chain.

adopted..claude/skills/spinoff/: taken with two translations, neither of which the closure check can see. The relative link to the source's catalog.md resolves to nothing here and reads as any catalog.md under .claude/skills/. And the stackless-vet rule it cites as CLAUDE.md § "Vetting" is the source's clause, declined here, so the skill states it itself. Everything else lands verbatim, its § "The watermark" pointer included: this repo carries the source's own name for the sync skill and for the watermark file, so the paragraph on what the target's copy is named holds here as written. Its catalog refusal needs no translation either — this repo has no catalog, which is exactly the signal that says a caller may spin off.

adopted..claude/hooks/: adopted whole. `install-deps.sh` ships upstream as a stub with a TODO where the install goes; here it carries this project's `corepack enable pnpm` + `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, so the source's edits to that file are read for the idea and the body never lands.

adopted.scripts/vet.sh: rewritten for this stack: pnpm build alone and first, then styles:codegen alone, then the rest fanned out through run-parallel.sh. CLAUDE.md § Vetting carries the roster and why each check sits where it does. Read the source's edits for the idea; the file itself never lands.

adopted..claude/skills/preview/: rewritten for this repo: one app booted through `pnpm --filter @kb/web dev`, its own route table, and no printed-page section, nothing here printing.
